type.A1.name: Bone-associated sealed compartments

physical.law: U_i = C_i^2/(2*kappa*V_0i); P_i = -dU_i/dV_i -- the existing water law derived independently per region
physical.player_moment: Press a calf: local pressure changes; neighbors respond through actual walls. Puncture it: the torso does not automatically drain.

falsifier.statement: A compartment that cannot remain sealed when its neighbor is punctured is not a compartment.

type.A2.name: Load-bearing outer skin

physical.law: U_s = int_S W_stretch dA + int_S W_bend dA; stretching stiffness ~ Et, bending ~ Et^3/[12(1-nu^2)]
physical.player_moment: Pressing, pinching, folding, and stretching produce consistent material responses.

falsifier.statement: A skin that cannot resist stretching cannot contain pressure.

type.A2.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item A2 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

type.A3.name: Septa, fascia, and sliding attachment layers

physical.law: Bonded attachments transmit traction; sliding interfaces resist interpenetration; compliant attachment U = 1/2 k ||dx||^2
physical.player_moment: Skin slides over a bending joint; pulling one patch loads a surrounding area.

falsifier.statement: An attachment that cannot slip or detach cannot demonstrate attachment strength.

type.A3.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item A3 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

type.A4.name: Structural bone walls

physical.law: Reduced beam: U = 1/2 int (EA eps^2 + EI chi^2) ds; distinct from the bone-associated water region
physical.player_moment: A limb resists bending; an overloaded structural member fractures.

falsifier.statement: A bone that cannot bend or break cannot teach bone strength.

type.A4.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item A4 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

type.A5.name: Joint capsules

physical.law: Capsule enclosing the articulation, attachment rims, fluid cavity; tau = -dU_capsule/dtheta
physical.player_moment: Bending stretches the capsule; excessive loading can destabilize the articulation.

falsifier.statement: A joint whose restraints cannot fail cannot demonstrate dislocation.

type.A5.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item A5 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

type.A6.name: Cartilage and lubricated bearing surfaces

physical.law: Darcy flow q = -(k_perm/mu) grad p; contact and lubrication set tangential resistance
physical.player_moment: A loaded joint cushions, creeps, and moves differently when lubrication is impaired.

falsifier.statement: A bearing whose motion never changes with load or lubrication cannot teach lubrication.

type.A6.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item A6 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

type.A7.name: Active contractile tissue

physical.law: F = a Fmax f_l(l) f_v(ldot) + F_passive; adot = (u-a)/tau_a; work from an explicit energy source
physical.player_moment: An obstructed muscle develops tension; faster shortening reduces force; opposing muscles stiffen a joint.

falsifier.statement: A muscle that cannot stall under load cannot demonstrate contraction.

type.A7.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item A7 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

physical.player_moment: Pulling a tendon moves its attached segment; cutting it removes that particular force path.

falsifier.statement: A tendon that can be cut without interrupting force transmission is not a tendon.

type.A8.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item A8 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

type.A9.name: Vessels, pump chambers, and valves

physical.player_moment: Squeeze a vessel, obstruct flow, feel a pulse, or observe downstream supply loss.

falsifier.statement: A circulation that cannot be interrupted cannot demonstrate circulation.

type.A9.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item A9 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

type.A10.name: Respiratory sacs, diaphragm, and airways

physical.player_moment: A torso expands; restraint reduces excursion; airway obstruction changes the cycle.

falsifier.statement: A breath that cannot be obstructed cannot demonstrate breathing.

type.A10.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item A10 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

falsifier.statement: A gut that produces nourishment without consuming anything cannot demonstrate digestion.

type.A12.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item A12 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

falsifier.statement: A glue joint that cannot fail at its interface cannot demonstrate adhesion.

type.B14.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item B14 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

falsifier.statement: A web that cannot redistribute load after a break cannot demonstrate a web.

type.B15.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item B15 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

type.B16.name: Yielding, scratches, and wear

physical.player_moment: A hard tool leaves a persistent groove in softer material.

falsifier.statement: A scratch that disappears on unloading cannot demonstrate plastic damage.

type.B16.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item B16 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

type.B17.name: Cracks, rupture, puncture, and delamination

physical.law: Cohesive zone: G_c = int_0^deltaf t(delta) d(delta); strength initiates, fracture energy separates
physical.player_moment: A puncture leaks; a tear spreads; a peeled layer loses attachment.

falsifier.statement: A rupture that leaves every physical connection intact is only a damage counter.

type.B17.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item B17 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

type.B18.name: Pores, holes, selective permeability, and leakage

physical.player_moment: Hole size and pressure affect leakage; later, water passes a barrier that retains solute.

falsifier.statement: A hole through which nothing can pass cannot demonstrate permeability.

type.B18.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item B18 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

physical.player_moment: Seal a leak and reload the repair; a weak patch can peel off.

falsifier.statement: A repair that cannot leak or fail under renewed load cannot demonstrate repair quality.

type.B19.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item B19 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

type.B20.name: Thermal boundaries, dissipation, and phase change

physical.player_moment: Repeated work warms tissue; heated glue cures differently; ice melts.

falsifier.statement: An actuator that delivers unlimited work without an energy source cannot teach energy.

type.B20.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item B20 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

type.B21.name: Growth, fission, and actual mitosis

physical.player_moment: Feed material to a compartment; it grows, deforms, and eventually divides.

falsifier.statement: A split that creates membrane and contents for free cannot demonstrate growth.

type.B21.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item B21 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

type.B22.name: Molecular membranes and chemical machinery

physical.player_moment: Osmotic swelling, ion gradients, selective transport, photosynthetic conversion.

falsifier.statement: A selective membrane with no selectivity cannot demonstrate a cell membrane.

type.B22.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item B22 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

type.C23.name: Ground contact and supporting substrate

physical.player_moment: Standing, slipping, pushing off, falling, leaving an indentation.

falsifier.statement: A ground that cannot let a foot slip cannot teach traction.

type.C23.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item C23 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

physical.player_moment: Water spills, pools, sloshes, displaces around a limb, supports floating objects.

falsifier.statement: A liquid surface that cannot rearrange when displaced cannot demonstrate liquid.

type.C24.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item C24 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

type.C25.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item C25 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

physical.player_moment: A gust pushes the creature; a pressure wave reaches it after a delay.

falsifier.statement: A wind that moves the creature without exchanging momentum cannot teach wind.

type.C26.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item C26 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

physical.player_moment: Catch leaked water, tie a support, press with different tips, patch a wound.

falsifier.statement: A container that cannot spill cannot demonstrate containment.

physical.law: Crusts as elastic/plastic shells; Newtonian gravity laplacian(Phi) = 4 pi G rho; an event horizon is a causal boundary
physical.player_moment: Eventually connect shell mechanics to planetary structure and gravity to larger scales.

falsifier.statement: A change of scale that changes the conservation laws without disclosure cannot teach scale.

type.D29.name: Local tactile receptor surfaces

physical.law: s = (1/A) int_A t_n dA followed by specified filtering, saturation, thresholding
physical.player_moment: The creature answers a calf press differently from a torso press or a broad squeeze.

falsifier.statement: A touch response that survives disconnecting its touch sensor cannot demonstrate sensing.

type.D29.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item D29 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

type.D30.name: Proprioception, load sensing, and balance sensing

physical.law: Sensors measure joint configuration, tissue extension, tendon force, angular motion, specific force -- separate observables
physical.player_moment: A loaded limb braces, an unsupported foot searches, a leaning body attempts recovery.

falsifier.statement: A balance controller that knows an unmeasured state perfectly cannot demonstrate embodied feedback.

type.D30.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item D30 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

type.D31.name: Axonal membranes and propagation

physical.law: Cable model C_j Vdot_j = sum_k (V_k - V_j)/R_jk - I_ion + I_input; cheap abstraction: event travel time L/v + refractory state
physical.player_moment: A distal stimulus produces a delayed response; interrupting the path removes it.

falsifier.statement: A nerve that transmits across a cut cannot demonstrate a nerve.

type.D31.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item D31 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

type.D32.name: Synapses, reflex integration, and adaptation

physical.law: tau sdot = -s + sum w_i input_i -- chosen reduced circuit dynamics with threshold, decay, adaptation
physical.player_moment: A rapid tap startles, sustained load braces, repeated harmless taps habituate.

falsifier.statement: A reflex whose response is unchanged by severing its sensory path cannot demonstrate a reflex.

type.D32.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item D32 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

type.D33.name: Eyes: optical boundary, sensor, eyelid, and gaze actuator

physical.law: Aperture + photosensitive surface; honest minimum: eye-local visibility sensor with FOV, occlusion, delay, bounded gaze
physical.player_moment: The creature notices the in-world hand, looks toward it, loses new evidence when hidden.

falsifier.statement: An eye that acquires new information through an opaque cover cannot demonstrate sight.

type.D33.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item D33 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

type.D34.name: Eardrums and vibration sensors

physical.law: m_e xddot + c_e xdot + k_e x = A_e dp -- force balance
physical.player_moment: A sound or ground vibration causes a response with direction- and distance-dependent timing.

falsifier.statement: An ear that hears equally well when acoustically isolated cannot demonstrate hearing.

type.D34.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item D34 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

physical.player_moment: The creature detects a nearby chemical source or reacts after touching something warm.

falsifier.statement: A receptor that responds without its stimulus reaching it cannot demonstrate reception.

type.D35.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item D35 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

type.E36.name: Player-to-world mechanical interface

physical.law: Finite force over finite footprint; F = k_h(x_t - x) + c_h(v_t - v) with declared caps; W = int F.dx
physical.player_moment: Press, hold, release, pull, and compare tools.

falsifier.statement: A press that deforms geometry without applying the corresponding load cannot teach force.

type.E36.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item E36 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

type.E37.name: Simulation-to-browser state boundary

physical.law: Displayed deformation/pressure/response refer to consistent authoritative states; timestamps + topology versions; interpolation invents nothing
physical.player_moment: The dimple, pressure rise, and flinch visibly agree.

falsifier.statement: A displayed response that precedes its authoritative cause cannot teach causality.

type.E37.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item E37 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

type.E38.name: Measurement and explanation interface

physical.law: Every shown quantity has units, provenance, model assumptions, appropriate precision; damping/aliasing disclosed
physical.player_moment: Open a cross-section, select one compartment, explain why its pressure changed.

falsifier.statement: A measurement that cannot be checked against an independent calculation cannot teach measurement.

type.E38.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item E38 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

type.E39.name: Import, sealing, and resolution boundary

physical.law: Imported geometry acquires valid regions, materials, attachments, sensor locations; refinement preserves mass
physical.player_moment: A new creature works for understandable geometric reasons.

falsifier.statement: An importer that passes only before the first joint bends has not imported a physical creature.

type.E39.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item E39 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

type.E40.name: Persistence, replay, and topology history

physical.law: Saving preserves fluid inventories, rest geometry, wounds, cure, activation, delayed signals, stable region identities
physical.player_moment: Return to the same wounded creature and continue the experiment.

falsifier.statement: A wound that disappears on reload is not persistent damage.

type.E40.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item E40 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

type.E41.name: Lesson and counterfactual boundary

physical.law: Success depends on the taught mechanism; ablations and transfer tests; confounders controlled
physical.player_moment: Predict which chamber leaks, which tendon moves the limb, whether a patch holds.

falsifier.statement: A lesson passed equally well after disabling its claimed law does not teach that law.

type.E41.notes: membrane TYPE from docs/THE_MEMBRANE_INVENTORY.md item E41 (Astra, 2026-09-15); reusable concept, not a creature part

type.E42.name: Creature-care loop and value gate

physical.player_moment: Notice, press, receive an answer, investigate, change something, see a lasting consequence.

falsifier.statement: A creature whose "aliveness" survives replacing feedback with disconnected replay has not yet proved responsive aliveness.

ref.uberon.UBERON_0001012.name: head of radius
ref.uberon.UBERON_0001012.definition: The head of the radius has a cylindrical form, and on its upper surface is a shallow cup or fovea for articulation with the capitulum (or capitellum) of the humerus. The circumference of the head is smooth; it is broad medially where it articulates with the radial notch of the ulna, narrow in the rest of its extent, which is embraced by the annular ligament. The deepest point in the fovea is not axi-symmetric with the long axis of the radius, creating a cam effect during pronation and supination[WP].

ref.uberon.UBERON_0001269.name: acetabular part of hip bone
ref.uberon.UBERON_0001269.definition: The acetabulum is a concave surface of the pelvis. The head of the femur meets with the pelvis at the acetabulum, forming the hip joint. There are three bones of the os coxae (hip bone) that come together to form the acetabulum. Contributing a little more than two-fifths of the structure is the ischium, which provides lower and side boundaries to the acetabulum. The ilium forms the upper boundary, providing a little less than two-fifths of the structure of the acetabulum. The rest is formed by the pubis, near the midline. It is bounded by a prominent uneven rim, which is thick and strong above, and serves for the attachment of the acetabular labrum, which reduces its opening, and deepens the surface for formation of the hip joint. At the lower part of the acetabulum is the acetabular notch, which is continuous with a circular depression, the acetabular fossa, at the bottom of the cavity of the acetabulum. The rest of the acetabulum is formed by a curved, crescent-moon shaped surface, the lunate surface, where the joint is made with the head of the femur. Its counterpart in the pectoral girdle is the glenoid fossa.[WP,unvetted].

ref.uberon.UBERON_0002495.name: long bone
ref.uberon.UBERON_0002495.definition: "A long bone is a bone that has a shaft and 2 ends and is longer than it is wide. Long bones have a thick outside layer of compact bone and an inner medullary cavity containing bone marrow.  The ends of a long bone contain spongy bone and an epiphyseal plate or line depending on the stage of development. The epiphyseal plate is a hyaline cartilage, where new bone growth takes place, lengthening the bone prior to adulthood. Bone lengthening ceases when this cartilage is lost, leaving a remnant referred to as an epiphyseal line." [https://medlineplus.gov/ency/imagepages/9582.htm, Wikipedia:Long_bone] {seeAlso="https://github.com/obophenotype/uberon/issues/32", seeAlso="https://github.com/obophenotype/uberon/issues/2010"}

Because the pelvic outlet in the female is larger than in the male, there is a greater distance between the greater trochanters in the female. It has two surfaces and four borders. [WP,unvetted].

ref.uberon.UBERON_0006767.name: head of femur
ref.uberon.UBERON_0006767.definition: The hemispheric articular surface at the upper extremity of the thigh bone[Stedman, 26th ed]. The femur head is the highest part of the thigh bone. It is supported by the neck of the femur. The head is globular and forms rather more than a hemisphere, is directed upward, medialward, and a little forward, the greater part of its convexity being above and in front. Its surface is smooth, coated with cartilage in the fresh state, except over an ovoid depression, the fovea capitis femoris, which is situated a little below and behind the center of the head, and gives attachment to the ligament of head of femur. If there is a fracture of the neck of the femur, the blood supply through the ligament becomes crucial. In orthopedic surgery, the head of the femur is important because it can undergo avascular necrosis and consequent osteochondritis dissecans. The head is removed in total hip replacement surgery [WP].

ref.uberon.UBERON_0006810.name: olecranon
ref.uberon.UBERON_0006810.definition: The olecranon is a large, thick, curved bony eminence of the forearm that projects behind the elbow. It is situated at the upper (proximal) end of the ulna, one of the two bones in the forearm. When the hand faces forward the olecranon faces towards the back (posteriorly). It is bent forward at the summit so as to present a prominent lip which is received into the olecranon fossa of the humerus in extension of the forearm. Its base is contracted where it joins the body and the narrowest part of the upper end of the ulna. Its posterior surface, directed backward, is triangular, smooth, subcutaneous, and covered by a bursa. Its superior surface is of quadrilateral form, marked behind by a rough impression for the insertion of the Triceps brachii; and in front, near the margin, by a slight transverse groove for the attachment of part of the posterior ligament of the elbow-joint. Its anterior surface is smooth, concave, and forms the upper part of the semilunar notch. Its borders present continuations of the groove on the margin of the superior surface; they serve for the attachment of ligaments, viz. , the back part of the ulnar collateral ligament medially, and the posterior ligament laterally. From the medial border a part of the Flexor carpi ulnaris arises; while to the lateral border the anconeus muscle is attached.

ref.uberon.UBERON_0007173.name: lateral border of scapula
ref.uberon.UBERON_0007173.definition: The lateral border (or axillary border, or margin) is the thickest of the three borders of the scapula. It begins above at the lower margin of the glenoid cavity, and inclines obliquely downward and backward to the inferior angle. Immediately below the glenoid cavity is a rough impression, the infraglenoid tuberosity, about 2.5 cm. in length, which gives origin to the long head of the Triceps brachii; in front of this is a longitudinal groove, which extends as far as the lower third of this border, and affords origin to part of the Subscapularis. The inferior third is thin and sharp, and serves for the attachment of a few fibers of the Teres major behind, and of the Subscapularis in front.

ref.uberon.UBERON_0007174.name: medial border of scapula
ref.uberon.UBERON_0007174.definition: The medial border of the scapula (vertebral border, medial margin) is the longest of the three borders, and extends from the medial to the inferior angle. It is arched, intermediate in thickness between the superior and the axillary borders, and the portion of it above the spine forms an obtuse angle with the part below. This border presents an anterior and a posterior lip, and an intermediate narrow area. The anterior lip affords attachment to the Serratus anterior; the posterior lip, to the Supraspinatus above the spine, the Infraspinatus below; the area between the two lips, to the Levator scapulC& above the triangular surface at the commencement of the spine, to the Rhomboideus minor on the edge of that surface, and to the Rhomboideus major below it; this last is attached by means of a fibrous arch, connected above to the lower part of the triangular surface at the base of the spine, and below to the lower part of the border.

ref.uberon.UBERON_0007831.name: pectoral girdle skeleton
ref.uberon.UBERON_0007831.definition: A subdivision of a limb or fin skeleton consisting of bones which connects the upper limb or fin to the axial skeleton on each side. It consists of the clavicle and scapula in humans and, in those species with three bones in the pectoral girdle, the coracoid. Some mammalian species (e.g. the dog and the horse) have only the scapula. In humans, the only joints between the shoulder girdle and axial skeleton are the sternoclavicular joints on each side. No joint exists between each scapula and the rib cage; instead the muscular connection between the two permits relatively great mobility of the shoulder girdle in relation to the pelvic girdle. In those species having only the scapula, no joint exists between the forelimb and the thorax, the only attachment being muscular[WP]. Examples: There are only two instances, right and left pectoral girdle skeletons.

ref.uberon.UBERON_0008194.name: tibiotarsus
ref.uberon.UBERON_0008194.definition: The tibiotarsus is the large bone between the femur and the tarsometatarsus in the leg of a bird. It is the fusion of the proximal part of the tarsus with the tibia. A similar structure also occurred in the Mesozoic Heterodontosauridae. These small ornithischian dinosaurs were unrelated to birds and the similarity of their pes bones is best explained by convergent evolution.

ref.uberon.UBERON_0008195.name: tarsometatarsus

It is formed from the fusion of several bones found in other types of animals, and homologous to the mammalian tarsal (ankle) and metatarsal (pes) bones. Despite this, the tarsometatarsus of birds is often referred to as just the tarsus or metatarsus.

ref.uberon.UBERON_0008449.name: trochlear notch
ref.uberon.UBERON_0008449.definition: The semilunar notch of the ulna (trochlear notch of ulna, greater sigmoid cavity) is a large depression, formed by the olecranon and the coronoid process, and serving for articulation with the trochlea of the humerus. About the middle of either side of this notch is an indentation, which contracts it somewhat, and indicates the junction of the olecranon and the coronoid process. The notch is concave from above downward, and divided into a medial and a lateral portion by a smooth ridge running from the summit of the olecranon to the tip of the coronoid process. ref.uberon.UBERON_0009984.name: medial condyle of femur
ref.uberon.UBERON_0009984.definition: The medial condyle is one of the two projections on the lower extremity of femur. The medial condyle is larger than the lateral (outer) condyle due to more weight bearing caused by the center of gravity being medial to the knee. On the posterior surface of the condyle the linea aspera (a ridge running down the posterior shaft of the femur) turns into the medial supracondylar ridge. The outermost protrusion on the medial surface of the medial condyle is referred to as the 'medial epicondyle' and can be palpated by running fingers medially from the patella with the knee in flexion.

ref.uberon.UBERON_0009985.name: lateral condyle of femur

Directly below it is a small depression from which a smooth well-marked groove curves obliquely upward and backward to the posterior extremity of the condyle.
ref.uberon.UBERON_0009986.notes: EXTRACTED: Uberon states it; not a creature part, not physically verified. Human anatomy is REFERENCE, never automatically Chimera proportions.

ref.uberon.UBERON_0009987.name: medial epicondyle of femur
ref.uberon.UBERON_0009987.definition: The medial epicondyle of the femur is a bony protrusion located on the medial side of the bone's distal end. Located above the medial condyle, it bears an elevation, the adductor tubercle, which serves for the attachment of the superficial part, or 'tendinous insertion', of the adductor magnus. This tendinous part here forms an intermuscular septum which forms the medial separation between the thigh's flexors and extensors. Behind it, and proximally to the medial condyle is a rough impression which gives origin to the medial head of the Gastrocnemius.

ref.uberon.UBERON_0010544.name: metacarpus skeleton
ref.uberon.UBERON_0010544.definition: The metacarpus is the intermediate part of the manus skeleton that is located between the phalanges (bones of the fingers) distally and the carpus which forms the connection to the forearm. The metacarpus consists of metacarpal bones. The metacarpals form a transverse arch to which the rigid row of distal carpal bones are fixed. The peripheral metacarpals (those of the thumb and little finger) form the sides of the cup of the palmar gutter and as they are brought together they deepen this concavity. The index metacarpal is the most firmly fixed, while the thumb metacarpal articulates with the trapezium and acts independently from the others. The middle metacarpals are tightly united to the carpus by intrinsic interlocking bone elements at their bases. The ring metacarpal forms a transitional element of the semi-independent last metacarpal. [WP,unvetted].

ref.uberon.UBERON_0011187.name: ventral tubercle of humerus
ref.uberon.UBERON_0011187.definition: The greater tubercle of the humerus is situated lateral to the head of the humerus and posteriolateral to the lesser tubercle. The lateral surface of the greater tubercle is convex, rough, and continuous with the lateral surface of the body. It also marks a vertex of the anal triangle and the urogenital triangle. The fascia of Colles is attached to its margin.
synonyms: rami of the pubis and ischium

ref.uberon.UBERON_0014442.name: superior ischial ramus
ref.uberon.UBERON_0014442.definition: The superior ramus of the ischium (descending ramus) projects downward and backward from the body and presents for examination three surfaces: external, internal, and posterior. The external surface is quadrilateral in shape. It is bounded above by a groove which lodges the tendon of the Obturator externus; below, it is continuous with the inferior ramus; in front it is limited by the posterior margin of the obturator foramen; behind, a prominent margin separates it from the posterior surface. In front of this margin the surface gives origin to the Quadratus femoris, and anterior to this to some of the fibers of origin of the Obturator externus; the lower part of the surface gives origin to part of the Adductor magnus. The internal surface forms part of the bony wall of the lesser pelvis. In front it is limited by the posterior margin of the obturator foramen. Below, it is bounded by a sharp ridge which gives attachment to a falciform prolongation of the sacrotuberous ligament, and, more anteriorly, gives origin to the Transversus perinC&i and Ischiocavernosus. Posteriorly the ramus forms a large swelling, the tuberosity of the ischium.
ref.uberon.UBERON_0014442.notes: EXTRACTED: Uberon states it; not a creature part, not physically verified. Human anatomy is REFERENCE, never automatically Chimera proportions.

ref.uberon.UBERON_0014443.name: inferior ischial ramus
ref.uberon.UBERON_0014443.definition: The Inferior Ramus of the ischium (ascending ramus) is the thin, flattened part of the ischium, which ascends from the superior ramus, and joins the inferior ramus of the pubisbthe junction being indicated in the adult by a raised line. The outer surface is uneven for the origin of the obturator externus and some of the fibers of the adductor magnus; its inner surface forms part of the anterior wall of the pelvis. Its medial border is thick, rough, slightly everted, forms part of the outlet of the pelvis, and presents two ridges and an intervening space. The ridges are continuous with similar ones on the inferior ramus of the pubis: to the outer is attached the deep layer of the superficial perineal fascia (fascia of Colles), and to the inner the inferior fascia of the urogenital diaphragm. If these two ridges be traced downward, they will be found to join with each other just behind the point of origin of the transversus perinC&i; here the two layers of fascia are continuous behind the posterior border of the muscle. To the intervening space, just in front of the point of junction of the ridges, the transversus perinC&i is attached, and in front of this a portion of the crus penis vel clitoridis and the ischiocavernosus. Its lateral border is thin and sharp, and forms part of the medial margin of the obturator foramen.

ref.uberon.UBERON_0014445.name: acetabular fossa
ref.uberon.UBERON_0014445.definition: The acetabular fossa is the roughened depression in the centre of the acetabulum, surrounded by the lunate acetabular surface and the acetabular notch. The acetabular fossa provides an insertion point for the teres ligaments that secure the femoral head.
ref.uberon.UBERON_0014445.notes: EXTRACTED: Uberon states it; not a creature part, not physically verified. Human anatomy is REFERENCE, never automatically Chimera proportions.

ref.uberon.UBERON_0014446.name: acetabular notch
ref.uberon.UBERON_0014446.definition: The acetabulum presents below a deep notch, the acetabular notch, which is continuous with a circular non-articular depression, the acetabular fossa, at the bottom of the cavity: this depression is perforated by numerous apertures, and lodges a mass of fat. The notch is converted into a foramen by the transverse ligament; through the foramen nutrient vessels and nerves enter the joint; the margins of the notch serve for the attachment of the ligament of the head of the femur.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200042.name: fibular facet of tibia

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200123.definition: A skeletal element projection forming the smaller, more lateral of the two inferior prominences of the calcaneal tuberosity. It provides attachment for the abductor digiti minimi muscle and the lateral slip of the plantar aponeurosis.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200128.name: lunate surface of os coxa
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200128.definition: A zone of bone organ forming the crescent-shaped articular cartilage-covered surface within the acetabulum of the os coxa (innominate bone), lining the peripheral rim of the acetabular socket and articulating directly with the head of the femur, with the non-articular acetabular fossa occupying the central gap.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200140.name: medial malleolus of tibia
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200140.definition: A skeletal element projection forming the prominent bony process that descends from the medial aspect of the distal tibia, constituting the medial wall of the ankle mortise. Its lateral surface bears a comma-shaped articular facet for the medial surface of the talar body, and its apex and posterior groove give attachment to the deltoid ligament complex and tendons of the deep posterior compartment, respectively.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200141.name: medial process of tuberosity of calcaneus
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200141.definition: A skeletal element projection forming the larger, more medial of the two inferior prominences of the calcaneal tuberosity. It is the principal origin of the plantar aponeurosis and provides attachment for the abductor hallucis, flexor digitorum brevis, and the plantar calcaneonavicular (spring) ligament.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200148.name: neck of radius of radius
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200148.definition: A zone of bone organ comprising the short, constricted segment of the radius immediately distal to the head, connecting the head to the radial tuberosity and serving as the site of attachment of the annular ligament.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200160.name: obturator groove of pubis of os coxa
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200160.definition: A surface groove forming the oblique channel running along the inferior surface of the superior pubic ramus of the pubis of the os coxa (innominate bone), roofed by the obturator membrane to form the obturator canal through which the obturator nerve and vessels pass from the pelvis to the thigh.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200166.name: pecten pubis of pubis of os coxa
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200166.definition: A zone of bone organ forming the sharp, ridge-like superior border of the superior pubic ramus of the pubis of the os coxa (innominate bone), extending from the pubic tubercle to the iliopectineal eminence and forming part of the pelvic brim, with the pectineus muscle attaching to its anterior surface.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200167.name: pectinal line of femur
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200167.definition: A zone of bone organ forming a raised ridge on the posterior surface of the proximal femoral shaft, running obliquely from the base of the lesser trochanter to the medial lip of the linea aspera. It serves as the insertion site for the pectineus muscle.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200174.name: posterior gluteal line of ilium of os coxa
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200174.definition: A zone of bone organ forming a curved ridge near the posterior margin of the gluteal surface of the ilium of the os coxa (innominate bone), extending from the iliac crest toward the greater sciatic notch and demarcating the small posterior area of origin of the gluteus maximus from the larger area of the gluteus medius.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200182.name: pubic body of pubis of os coxa
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200182.definition: A zone of bone organ forming the flattened, medial main portion of the pubis of the os coxa (innominate bone), presenting a medial symphyseal surface that articulates with the contralateral pubic body at the pubic symphysis and a superior surface bearing the pubic crest and pubic tubercle.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200183.name: pubic crest of pubis of os coxa
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200183.definition: A crest forming the thick, rough, horizontal ridge on the superior surface of the pubic body of the pubis of the os coxa (innominate bone), extending medially from the pubic tubercle to the pubic symphysis and providing attachment for the rectus abdominis and pyramidalis muscles.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200185.name: pubic tubercle of pubis of os coxa
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200185.definition: A skeletal element projection forming a small but prominent rounded eminence on the superior border of the pubic body of the pubis of the os coxa (innominate bone), situated lateral to the pubic symphysis and serving as the medial attachment of the inguinal ligament and a landmark for the superficial inguinal ring.
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200185.notes: EXTRACTED: Uberon states it; not a creature part, not physically verified. Human anatomy is REFERENCE, never automatically Chimera proportions.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200186.name: radial fossa of humerus
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200186.definition: A bone fossa situated on the anterior surface of the lateral distal humerus, immediately superior to the capitulum, that receives the anterior rim of the head of the radius during full flexion of the elbow at the humeroradial joint.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200187.name: radial groove of humerus
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200187.definition: A surface groove spiraling obliquely across the posterior surface of the humeral shaft from the medial to the lateral side, separating the origins of the medial and lateral heads of the triceps brachii. It transmits the radial nerve and the deep brachial artery, and is also termed the musculospiral groove.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200188.name: radial tuberosity of radius
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200188.definition: A skeletal element projection forming the oval, roughened eminence on the medial aspect of the radius just distal to the neck, serving as the distal insertion point of the biceps brachii tendon.
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200188.notes: EXTRACTED: Uberon states it; not a creature part, not physically verified. Human anatomy is REFERENCE, never automatically Chimera proportions.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200197.name: scaphoid tubercle of scaphoid
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200197.definition: A skeletal element projection on the palmar surface of the scaphoid bone at its distal pole, forming the lateral pillar of the carpal tunnel and serving as an attachment point for the flexor retinaculum and the abductor pollicis brevis muscle.
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200197.notes: EXTRACTED: Uberon states it; not a creature part, not physically verified. Human anatomy is REFERENCE, never automatically Chimera proportions.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200198.name: scapular notch of scapula
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200198.definition: A semicircular bone foramen on the superior border of the scapula, medial to the base of the coracoid process, through which the suprascapular nerve passes beneath the superior transverse scapular ligament to enter the supraspinous fossa.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200199.name: scapular spine of scapula
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200199.definition: A prominent, triangular skeletal element projection arising from the posterior surface of the scapula and running obliquely from the medial border to the acromion, dividing the posterior scapular surface into the supraspinous and infraspinous fossae and providing attachment for the trapezius and deltoid muscles.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200201.name: shaft of first distal phalanx of hand
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200201.definition: A zone of bone organ comprising the flattened, tapering body of the distal phalanx of the thumb, lying between the base and the ungual tuberosity and providing dorsal and palmar surfaces for attachment of the nail bed and soft tissue pulp.
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200201.notes: EXTRACTED: Uberon states it; not a creature part, not physically verified. Human anatomy is REFERENCE, never automatically Chimera proportions.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200202.name: shaft of first proximal phalanx of hand
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200202.definition: A zone of bone organ comprising the elongated cylindrical body of the proximal phalanx of the thumb, connecting the base to the head and providing attachment surfaces for the flexor and extensor tendons of the thumb.
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200202.notes: EXTRACTED: Uberon states it; not a creature part, not physically verified. Human anatomy is REFERENCE, never automatically Chimera proportions.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200203.name: shaft of radius of radius
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200203.definition: A zone of bone organ comprising the elongated body of the radius between the radial tuberosity proximally and the distal epiphysis, prismatic in cross-section with a sharp interosseous border medially that gives attachment to the interosseous membrane.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200204.name: shaft of ulna of ulna
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200204.definition: A zone of bone organ comprising the elongated body of the ulna between the coronoid process proximally and the head distally, triangular in cross-section with a sharp lateral interosseous border that provides attachment for the interosseous membrane.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200205.name: soleal line of tibia
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200205.definition: A zone of bone organ forming an oblique ridge on the posterior surface of the proximal tibial shaft, running from the fibular facet of the lateral condyle downward and medially to the medial border of the tibia. It marks the proximal attachment of the soleus muscle and the transverse intermuscular septum separating the superficial and deep posterior compartments of the leg.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200257.name: supinator fossa of ulna
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200257.definition: A bone fossa forming the concave depression on the lateral aspect of the proximal ulna, just distal to the radial notch, providing the origin for the deep fibres of the supinator muscle.
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200257.notes: EXTRACTED: Uberon states it; not a creature part, not physically verified. Human anatomy is REFERENCE, never automatically Chimera proportions.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200261.name: supraspinous fossa of scapula
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200261.definition: A triangular bone fossa on the posterior surface of the scapula superior to the scapular spine, providing origin for the supraspinatus muscle, whose tendon passes beneath the coracoacromial arch to insert on the greater tubercle of the humerus.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200262.name: sustentaculum tali of calcaneus
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200262.definition: A zone of bone organ forming a horizontal, shelf-like medial projection of the calcaneus that supports the head and neck of the talus. Its superior surface bears the middle talar articular facet, its inferior surface is grooved for the tendon of the flexor hallucis longus, and it provides attachment for the plantar calcaneonavicular and medial talocalcaneal ligaments.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200264.name: tibial plateau of tibia
ref.uberon.UBERON_1200264.definition: A zone of bone organ comprising the expanded proximal articular surface of the tibia, consisting of the medial and lateral condyles, which together form the superior articular surface of the knee joint. Each condyle bears a meniscus-covered articular facet that articulates with the corresponding femoral condyle, and the two condyles are separated by the intercondylar eminence.

ref.uberon.UBERON_1200281.name: tuberosity of fifth distal phalanx of hand

ref.uberon.UBERON_1500000.name: scapular blade

ref.uberon.UBERON_3000941.name: arciferal girdle
ref.uberon.UBERON_3000941.definition: Pectoral girdle in which the epicoracoid cartilages are elaborated into posteriorly directed epicoracoid horns. Most arciferal pectoral girdles are characterized by fusion of the epicoracoid cartilages in the interclavicle region. Posterior to the clavicles, the epicoracoids usually are free and overlapping.
ref.uberon.UBERON_3000941.notes: EXTRACTED: Uberon states it; not a creature part, not physically verified. Human anatomy is REFERENCE, never automatically Chimera proportions.

ref.uberon.UBERON_3000942.name: firmisternal girdle
ref.uberon.UBERON_3000942.definition: Pectoral girdle that lacks epicoracoid horns. The sternum is fused to the pectoral arch, and the epicoracoid cartilages of each half of the girdle are fused to one another. The midzonal length of the girdle is shorter than that of an arciferal girdle, but pre- and postzonal elements tend to be longer.
ref.uberon.UBERON_3000942.notes: EXTRACTED: Uberon states it; not a creature part, not physically verified. Human anatomy is REFERENCE, never automatically Chimera proportions.

ref.uberon.UBERON_3000943.name: pseudofirmisternal girdle
